changes.title: Fast start bakes
items: The game opens faster: her room shows sooner while the witch, her treehouse and the soundsystems are drawn in the background

changes.title: Sprite quirks
items: Birds, bugs and the little creatures have idle habits too: owls look behind them, ravens hop, hedgehogs and snails puff up, moths and beetles shiver
From the treetops every creature shows its idle habit

changes.title: Sigil spill
items: Sigils you put down cast their colour on the ground and anyone near them
The sigil you carry tints you in its colour

changes.title: Sigil freeze
items: A freeze the first time a sigil showed (the leash's stack, a placed rune, a quest bubble) is gone: the game no longer reads that picture back from the graphics card mid-frame.

changes.title: Making of
items: The Making Of: a little website about how the game was built, at /making-of/ beside the game

changes.title: Ley curvature
items: The ley line never kinks: it sweeps through each runestone in one smooth curve and never turns tighter than 25 m (leyLines.minRadius); where the next stone lies back the way it came, it loops round the stone instead of doubling back in a hairpin

changes.title: Level gap
items: Grown-up creatures are now far stronger than young ones (about three and a half times), so evolving your animals to adult really pays, and the wild adults far from home hit harder
Young creatures are a little gentler, and young and adults take fewer 💌s to win over (7 and 14, from 9 and 18)
Evolving now costs 3 berries to young and 8 to adult (it was 4 and 4)
Add ?tuning=pre-overnight to the link to play the balance as it was before tonight

changes.title: Friendly area
items: Bringing a legend what it dreams of now makes its whole area friendly at once: the creatures already living there stop attacking her (any mid-fight calm down and drop their sieges), not only the ones grown there afterwards

changes.title: Big four shapes
items: Wolves stand taller and leaner on long legs, the adults with a shaggy mane
Badgers are low, wide and flat, on short thick legs
Boars carry a big shoulder hump and a heavy front end
Bears are massive, with a high shoulder hump and pillar legs

changes.title: Amphibian shapes
items: Newts carry a tall jagged crest along their backs
Salamanders sprawl low and stocky on short thick legs

changes.title: Ley front
items: The front of the ley line is a small pixel spark that pulses on the beat, with a soft little light and embers flying off as it writes the line; it flares as it reaches a stone, and you can spot it from the treetops
Ahead of the pulse the ley line is a faint dashed sketch; behind it, lit and glowing: you can see the pulse light it up as it goes
The ley line leaves the speaker ring from the ring itself, one path from the treehouse out into the forest, and shows the way out while home boots up
No more ley line showing through hills far off, and no more blown-out glare at its front

changes.title: Far dreams
items: A sleeping legend can still dream of a creature from anywhere, but never from the far side of the map
Quests whose creature lives far away now give a stronger buff, up to half again as strong

changes.title: Bend hides
items: Nothing on the ground shows through the curve of the world any more: invitations, hearts, chat bubbles and the angry and dazed marks past the horizon are hidden by the earth

changes.title: Attack alarm
items: A soundsystem (or the home ring's speakers) under attack off screen shows a 🔇 at the screen's edge pointing to it, drawn in pixels like the 🎶 pointer: its ring is the soundsystem's health, draining as it's hit, the cue shakes at each blow, it says how far, and it flashes and fades if the soundsystem falls; one per soundsystem, up to three, on the ground and from the treetops (?debug=attack to see it)
The edge pointers' distances are one crisp pixel label each: pointers that would sit on one another are moved apart along the edge, and each label sits clear of its ring

changes.title: Knockout respawn
items: Knocked out, your hat floats to the ground, then you scratch behind your decks until you can fly again: about six seconds in all, a little longer each time you are knocked down again soon after, a countdown over you, while your animals fight on without you
